speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the pattern of your symptoms, have you noticed any difficulty with swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of diplopia worsening with upward gaze and weakness improving with rest is highly suggestive of Myasthenia Gravis. To confirm this, I need to check your eye movements and test your muscle strength. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies and REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation. REQUEST IMAGES: Eye_Extraocular_Movement_Photo.

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The clinical presentation of fluctuating weakness, diplopia worsening with upward gaze, and ptosis, combined with elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies and decreased response on repetitive nerve stimulation, confirms this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder.
